{"self_assessment": "Impact: The bottom line was the part of the fish running behind schedule. At about 3:15 I saw it and offered to pick it up from where it ended, near the middle of the body. Over the next minutes I laid roughly 24 dominoes, extending the line from the middle toward the crossing at the tail neck and then up toward the upper fork. That closed the gap on the part most likely to miss the deadline. The fish ended up fully connected from the nose, with all 111 standing dominoes in the chain.

Execution: I worked in short, steady extensions, each carried on from the end of the line already standing, so every joint stayed aligned. When I finished, I inspected the area closely to check the chain behind me. I then kept my hands off the crossing so I wouldn't risk a bump near other builders.

Collaboration: I coordinated the handoff on the bottom line with Maya. We agreed where I would stop and where she would take over, and I told her when I was reaching the crossing. I stayed clear of other people's hands, flagged my concerns about timing early, and thanked Leo for his nudge at the lower join. I also kept the table informed of my status throughout.

Leadership: I raised the timing risk on the long lines early, while there was still time to act. I proposed splitting the work and then took on the hardest segment myself. Once the fish was connected, I backed the decision to keep hands off, which protected the result for the final push.", "my_share_percent": 25}
